title: Sunset of legacy-request-buffering endpoint and migration safety net
creator: Avery Chen
description: This ticket defines the plan to retire the legacy /v0/buffered-generate and /v0/buffered-stream endpoints (collectively: 'legacy-request-buffering') and to provide a migration safety net for clients that still rely on buffering semantics. The goal is a predictable, low-friction transition to the Unified Generate API with a staged sunset, client-side SDK helpers, clear telemetry gates, and an automated rollback corridor in case of regression.
background: Legacy-request-buffering was introduced as an interim for clients with intermittent connectivity and very long-polling producers. Over time we consolidated streaming and generate into the Unified Generate API. A minority of enterprise customers still have integrations that depend on buffered semantics and server-side batching behavior. We have telemetry showing ~0.9% of active keys use these endpoints primarily for retry/ordering guarantees. Continued support complicates runtime optimization and creates maintenance surface area.
scope: In scope: deprecation timeline, SDK migration helpers (JavaScript/Python/Go), server-side compatibility shim for a 6-12 month transitional window, telemetry and gates, customer communications, canonical migration guides, acceptance criteria, rollback procedures. Work to be coordinated across PM, Eng (runtime + API gateways), Design (docs & in-console messaging), and Solutions Engineering.
out_of_scope: Implementing new buffering semantics in the Unified API, major changes to existing enterprise contracts, cross-cloud region migrations, or full reimplementation of legacy SDKs.
requirements:
- Public deprecation notice published at least 90 days before enforcement.
- SDK helpers that translate buffered calls to Unified Generate with equivalent dedup/retry semantics.
- Server-side compatibility shim that accepts legacy payloads and translates to Unified Generate for a configurable duration.
- Telemetry events and dashboards tracking success rate, latency, and model-output divergence for shimmed requests.
- Canary metrics with automatic hold/rollback if error rate or output-quality regressions exceed thresholds.
- Migration playbook for customers with custom brokers or long-poll clients.
- Legal/compliance check for data retention/exposure during translation path.
- End-to-end tests and load tests validating throughput and SLOs under shimmed traffic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deprecation notice draft reviewed by Legal and comms and published to docs and changelog.
- SDK helper release (JS/Python/Go) with test coverage and migration samples.
- Compatibility shim deployed to a dark canary traffic class and validated against production-like traces.
- Dashboards present: volume by key, error rate delta (shim vs native), median/95th latency, and a divergence score comparing top-3 token deltas per response.
- Canary gate rules implemented: hold if error_rate_delta > 2% or divergence_score > configured threshold for 15 minutes.
- Migration guide with sample code, checklist, and troubleshooting published.
- Customer-impact review completed and top 10 affected customers have outreach plans assigned.
- Rollout runbook and rollback playbook documented and practiced in staging runbook exercise.
- Updated SDK changelog and migration CLI commands verified by Solutions Engineering on 3 customer integrations.
migration_timeline:
- T+0 (2025-03-10): Announce deprecation (90-day notice).
- T+14 days (2025-03-24): SDK helper alpha + docs draft open for review.
- T+30 days (2025-04-09): Compatibility shim deployed in internal dark canary; telemetry collection enabled.
- T+60 days (2025-05-09): Public beta of shim; invite top-10 customers to test migration.
- T+90 days (2025-06-08): Begin gradual enforcement: new keys blocked from creating new buffered sessions.
- T+120 days (2025-07-08): Enforcement: legacy endpoints return 410 for non-shimmed clients; shim remains for enrolled customers.
- T+240 days (2025-10-06): Full retirement; shim turned off and endpoints removed from gateway.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Internal validation and stakeholder sign-off.
Phase 1: Publish docs, release SDK helpers, enable telemetry.
Phase 2: Deploy shim to dark canary, monitor metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 3: Invite pilot customers, gather feedback, patch behaviors.
Phase 4: Soft enforcement for new sessions, continued customer outreach.
Phase 5: Full enforcement and final retirement schedule.
Each phase has explicit go/no-go criteria maintained in the release checklist.
rollback_plan: If canary gates trigger (error_rate_delta > 2% or divergence_score breaches), immediately: 1) Pause shim rollout and route affected traffic back to previous stable instance; 2) Revert any SDK publish flagged as problematic; 3) Notify stakeholder channel with incident summary and mitigation steps; 4) Run targeted hotfix in shim translator to address regression; 5) Resume canary only after postmortem and sign-off.
monitoring_and_telemetry:
- New telemetry keys: legacy_buffered.requests.total, legacy_buffered.requests.shimmed, legacy_buffered.error.rate, legacy_buffered.divergence.score, legacy_buffered.latency.p50/p95.
- Dashboard templates for PM/Eng/SE.
- Alerting rules: pager for >1% absolute increase in customer 5xx for 5m; SE channel for divergence_score spike.
- Sampling of raw payloads for manual review (controls in place to redact PII).
communications_plan:
- External: Documentation site banner, changelog entry, and email to affected keys at T+0. Webinars and migration office hours during T+14 to T+60.
- Internal: Slack #api-deprecations weekly updates, engineering standups, and release readiness doc in Confluence.
- Account teams: Prepared one-pagers and a migration checklist for Solutions Engineers to run for each affected account.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for SDK helper covering retry/dedup cases
Integration tests with shim in staging against recorded traces
Load test at 2x expected peak for shim translation logic
End-to-end regression test for Unified Generate equivalence
Documentation review and copy sign-off by Design
updates: 2025-02-20: Scoped initial compatibility-shim approach with ENG-58412; shim design doc linked.
2025-02-28: Legal reviewed deprecation language; minor edits requested around retention disclosure.
2025-03-03: Design provided banner mockups for docs and Console; DES-3110 assigned for implementation.
2025-03-05: Top-10 impacted account list compiled by Customer Success; outreach owners assigned.
notes_and_risks:
- Risk: Some high-throughput broker integrations rely on ordering semantics that are not trivially reproduced by Unified Generate; mitigation: provide per-account shim tuning and SE support.
- Risk: Translation path may increase token-cost billing surface for shimmed requests; mitigation: show comparative cost in dashboards and set billing alerts.
- Operational note: Ensure KMS/HSM integrations remain honored in shim path; involve Security & Compliance early.
